hook.text: Ransomware hit a company's cloud. Attackers encrypted everything and demanded $10 million in Bitcoin.

buildup.text: Cloud ransomware works by gaining access to admin credentials, then encrypting or deleting data and backups.

discovery.text: Attackers target cloud admin accounts because one compromise gives access to everything.

twist.text: Some ransomware groups skip encryption entirely. They just steal data and threaten to publish it.

climax.text: Preventing cloud ransomware requires MFA, least privilege, immutable backups, and constant monitoring.

punchline.text: Ransomware loves cloud admin accounts. Protect them above all.

quiz.question: Why are cloud admin accounts prime targets for ransomware?
options: One compromised admin account gives access to all cloud resources
Admin accounts always have the weakest passwords
Cloud admin accounts cannot have MFA enabled

details.summary: Cloud ransomware attacks encrypt cloud-hosted data or lock out administrators by hijacking cloud accounts. Attackers exploit compromised credentials, misconfigured access, or vulnerable applications to deploy ransomware across cloud storage, databases, and virtual machines.
details.whyItMatters: Ransomware has expanded beyond on-premises to target cloud environments. Organizations must prepare defenses specifically designed for cloud attack surfaces.
takeaways: Attackers target cloud accounts via stolen credentials
Cloud backups must be isolated from production access
MFA and least privilege are the strongest preventions

faq.question: How does ransomware spread in the cloud?
faq.answer: Attackers gain access through phished credentials, exploited vulnerabilities, or compromised service accounts. They then escalate privileges, disable backups, and encrypt data across connected storage and databases. Cloud-native ransomware can spread across regions in minutes.

faq.question: How should cloud backups be protected from ransomware?
faq.answer: Use immutable backup storage that cannot be deleted even by administrators. Store backups in separate accounts with independent credentials. Enable versioning on object storage and test restore procedures regularly so recovery is fast and reliable.
